study.question: Does a different, noninvolutive occupied-row permutation of auxiliary cotangents change the transported orientation bit and its click-AUC effect, after the half-batch source control reproduced both native-sign AUCs exactly?
study.hypothesis: The useful negative fixed-angle transfer may depend on how the auxiliary cotangent triple aligns with click/context rows when generating its single Q orientation bit. The last half-batch permutation may have retained that bit or sufficient structure; that explanation is unmeasured. A cyclic occupied-row donor mapping distinct from Q's inherited half-batch operator should perturb that correspondence while retaining the actual native radius, canonical line and support. If the negative native advantage depends on this source, the source-by-sign contrast should change after a verified bit intervention. This is a prospective causal probe, not a claim that the new donor model improves performance.

nearest_work.difference: Read archived exact-version primary lines245-284 (text SHA25683fb9eeca31e2fa3c557b6f08b893ad0018cefb33da6e00952136b9ce17e607e). Retain inherited target-conditioned unnormalized local activation and BCE adaptation. The present change is training-only cotangent-bit source replacement in the stronger imported model, not an exact DIN reproduction or a novelty claim.

The supplied native-source ancestor and paired-source module contain the same full-task fixed-angle forward model and training-loss graph. Change only the bit-source selector and add the same state-free occupied-cycle helper work to all arms; native bridges retain the old expression.

Replace the old occupied half-batch source permutation with rotation by max(1,floor(n_occupied/4)) within the ascending occupied index list. Keep the original half-batch operator used inside Q itself unchanged. This is a different correspondence probe, not a general label permutation.

Read cached primary benchmark section2.3 lines1-39. Its forward unified-interaction descriptions motivate no added architecture here. Original INFNet/TokenFormer/EST/HyFormer papers are not newly audited, and the nearest external gradient-method literature remains unverified.

inherited_components: Stronger joint product-fusion model and all feature embeddings, action-aware local activation, task towers, history compression, moment summaries and task adapters.
Folded attached support during training, fully pruned inference path and all native normalization/running-state updates.
FP64 occupied-row centering, click-relative split, native O radius, deterministic carriers, fixed-pi/4 nuisance line and inherited gates.
All-task joint BCE training_loss, private true-label gradients and four-output custom context-cotangent collector.
Previous bit-source helpers executed identically in every arm, with no new parameters, buffers or RNG.
study.proposed_difference: Add _occupied_cycle_donor_rows and _occupied_cycle_source_orientation_bit. Sort unique occupied-first row keys; assign each occupied rank r the donor (r+max(1,floor(n/4))) mod n and fix empty rows. Apply that same permutation to each auxiliary cotangent, recompute C/O/reassignment/Q using existing helpers and take the first maximal-absolute Q pivot sign (zero -> +1). Multiply ONLY the native full-task canonical fixed-angle transfer by that bit. The actual transfer radius/line/support and private losses never use donors. Cross this source choice with reversed/aligned external sign; both native bridges execute the extra helper too.
predictions: On fixed host states with at least three occupied rows the donor mapping is a bijection of occupied rows, is neither identity nor involution, fixes empty rows, and preserves each complete cart/fav/buy row triple multiset. It differs from the half-batch operator used to construct Q.

On representative fixed host states the new donor bit disagrees with the native bit on a nonzero fraction of active updates. This manipulation check is a prerequisite for interpreting a null contrast, not an assumed fact.

Before the single cast, actual donor/native transfers share support, canonical line and Frobenius norm at the same state; they differ by a global sign when their source bits differ. Private/forward graphs are unchanged at that state.

Native bridges should reproduce click AUC0.6689610675617089 (negative) and0.6683760511656333 (positive) under the frozen seed. Source-specific usefulness predicts the cycle source weakens the negative native advantage and changes S=AUC_negative-AUC_positive; predeclared interaction is S_cycle-S_native.
Added helper work raises training cost equally in all four cells; parameter count and inference graph remain inherited. No inference speed improvement is predicted.
falsifiers: If the source bits never differ on representative active host updates, the new operator has failed to manipulate the proposed mediator; no causal conclusion from equal AUC and no automatic further permutation sweep.

Any altered forward probabilities, loss values, private gradients or running-state update at a fixed state beyond declared tolerances, or any transfer norm/support mismatch, invalidates the intended bit-only comparison.
If the native bridges fail to reproduce the prior pair, attribution to source choice is suspended until host/source/numerical execution differences are resolved.

If meaningful bit changes are verified yet the cycle source retains the native negative benefit and sign gap across admissible paired repetitions/uncertainty checks, the claim that native row-source correspondence is necessary is not supported.

If the best permissible donor sign matches or exceeds the native negative model, a specifically native-source advantage is not supported. One favorable cell alone does not establish auxiliary semantic transfer.
Without host bit/geometry diagnostics, AUCs establish predictive contrasts only; the bit-correspondence mechanism stays unresolved regardless of the result.
alternative_explanations: Donor cotangents contain donor features/probabilities and batch/state dependencies; a deterministic permutation is not independent-label supervision.
Auxiliary information remains in transfer radius, inherited gates and private-task learning; this does not ablate all auxiliary-label information.
Different source bits need not occur. Latest source experiment has no gradient diagnostics; equal AUC cannot certify equal or changed updates.
Fixed-state line/norm support parity does not constrain later training states. Row-space orthogonality precedes dtype cast, repeated-ID scatter, clipping and adaptive optimization.
One frozen seed and many prior validation comparisons imply exploratory selection risk. Deterministic same-seed replays are not independent replication.
The occupied-cycle operator is chosen once to avoid the original half-batch involution. It is order dependent, not isotropic noise; n<=2 cannot provide a noninvolution contrast.
